en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Sublime Colors, Spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Official of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
"There is a dhāraṇī named 'Exquisite Color' (Varṇa),
which has been proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the three periods of time and is able to bring great benefit to sentient beings."
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who, upon hearing this dhāraṇī,
conceives the thought that it is difficult to encounter and gives rise to a courageous mind,
reading, reciting, receiving, upholding, making offerings to, and revering it.
Such a person will, in accordance with reason, obtain a great mass of merit in this world and remain secure day and night.
Furthermore, there are those who, with a heart of great compassion...
In a secluded place, holding various foods and drinks, one should bring them forth.
Reciting this dhāraṇī seven times and having empowered them, one speaks these words:
"I now offer this birth as a sacrifice to all the hungry ghosts of the evil realms in the world.
May those who consume this birth quickly depart from the evil realms.
As he spoke these words, he snapped his fingers three times.
Visualize that those various spirits who receive this food are each fully satiated;
their wondrous physical forms are transformed, they give rise to the bodhicitta,
and eventually, in the future, they gradually attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

*Namo bhagavate* (1) *sūraprabhāya* (2) *tathāgatāya* (3) *arhat-samyak-saṃbuddhāya* (4). *Tadyathā* (5): *Oṃ sūru sūru* (6) *prasūru prasūru* (7) *samara samara* (8) *para para* (9) *sapara sapara* (10) *sarva-pratibheda-viśodhanāya* (11) *āharaṇadana-mi svāhā* (12). At that time, Ānanda, having heard what the Buddha had spoken...
Rejoicing and receiving it with faith, they paid homage and withdrew.
Thus ends the *Sūtra on the Dharani of Wondrous Colors* spoken by the Buddha.
